### How the baby is *supposed* to age
The pet’s life stage is derived from `this.age` in seconds:

```112:116:/Users/esther/Code/tamagooglishi/src/entities/Pet.js
getStage() {
    if (this.age < 300) return 'BABY'; // 0-5 mins
    if (this.age < 900) return 'CHILD'; // 5-15 mins
    return 'ADULT'; // 15+ mins
}
```

The UI just displays that stage plus “minutes” as `Math.floor(age / 60)`:

```47:51:/Users/esther/Code/tamagooglishi/src/core/UI.js
if (this.elAge) {
    const stage = this.pet.getStage();
    const ageMins = Math.floor(this.pet.age / 60);
    this.elAge.innerText = `${stage} (${ageMins}m)`;
}
```

### How the baby actually ages *right now*
It **doesn’t**: `this.age` is initialized to `0` and **never incremented anywhere** in the game loop or `Pet.update()`. So `getStage()` will always return **`BABY`** unless a save file loads a non-zero age.

You can see age only being saved/loaded, not updated:

```231:244:/Users/esther/Code/tamagooglishi/src/entities/Pet.js
serialize() {
    return { stats: { ...this.stats }, state: this.state, age: this.age };
}

deserialize(data) {
    if (!data) return;
    if (data.stats) this.stats = { ...data.stats };
    if (data.state) this.state = data.state;
    if (data.age) this.age = data.age;
}
```

If you want, I can implement the missing increment (typically `this.age += delta/1000` in `Pet.update(delta)`), so the pet actually evolves from baby → child → adult over time.
